book_metadata.title: LIVE WELL: 8 habits to highly effective Health and Happiness
book_metadata.subtitle: A Modern Guide to Health, Longevity, and Disease Reversal
book_metadata.author: Dr. Murthy Gokula, MD, CMD, Dip ABLM, Dip FAAARM
book_metadata.co_authors: Laya Gokula, Vihana Shresta, Taarini Pappula, Neha Chanda
book_metadata.summary: A clinical and lifestyle medicine guide integrating the Six Pillars of Lifestyle Medicine, the Nine Hallmarks of Longevity, the 8 steps of Ashtanga Yoga, and the 'MY GOAL DO IT' microhabits framework to prevent and reverse chronic disease.

lifestyle_pillars.name: Nutrition
lifestyle_pillars.summary: Whole-food, plant-based diets rich in fiber, antioxidants, and colorful plants.
lifestyle_pillars.cellular_benefits: Reverses insulin resistance, reduces systemic cytokines (NF-κB, IL-6), feeds beneficial microbiome, and optimizes nutrient sensing.
lifestyle_pillars.clinical_evidence: American College of Lifestyle Medicine (ACLM), Harvard Medical School lifestyle medicine curricula.

lifestyle_pillars.name: Physical Activity
lifestyle_pillars.summary: Consistent daily movement combining aerobic activity (150 min/wk), strength training, and mobility.
lifestyle_pillars.cellular_benefits: Rejuvenates mitochondria, stimulates stem cell mobilization, flushes damaged proteins (autophagy), and enhances insulin sensitivity.
lifestyle_pillars.clinical_evidence: Aerobic + resistance training increases mitochondrial biogenesis (PGC-1α).

lifestyle_pillars.name: Restorative Sleep
lifestyle_pillars.summary: 7–9 hours of continuous, restorative sleep supporting slow-wave and REM cycles.
lifestyle_pillars.cellular_benefits: Maintains DNA repair mechanisms, protects telomere length, improves glymphatic brain waste clearance, and balances cortisol.
lifestyle_pillars.clinical_evidence: Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), Dawson & Reid sleep debt models.

lifestyle_pillars.name: Stress Management
lifestyle_pillars.summary: Mindfulness, diaphragmatic breathwork (Pranayama), yoga, and vagal nerve activation.
lifestyle_pillars.cellular_benefits: Lowers sympathetic overdrive, reduces HPA-axis cortisol spikes, protects prefrontal cortex executive control, and reduces DNA damage.
lifestyle_pillars.clinical_evidence: Yerkes-Dodson arousal law, McEwen's allostatic load model.

lifestyle_pillars.name: Avoidance of Harmful Substances
lifestyle_pillars.summary: Limiting alcohol, eliminating tobacco/vaping, and reducing environmental toxin exposure.
lifestyle_pillars.cellular_benefits: Decreases toxic load on liver and kidneys, prevents DNA adducts and cellular senescence, and protects mitochondrial membranes.
lifestyle_pillars.clinical_evidence: WHO and IARC environmental health guidelines.

lifestyle_pillars.name: Social Connection
lifestyle_pillars.summary: Fostering meaningful, loving relationships and community belonging.
lifestyle_pillars.cellular_benefits: Reduces loneliness, calms systemic inflammatory signaling, increases oxytocin, and enhances emotional resilience.
lifestyle_pillars.clinical_evidence: Harvard Study of Adult Development (longest longitudinal health study).

hallmarks_of_aging.name: Genomic Instability
hallmarks_of_aging.biological_mechanism: Accumulation of DNA lesions and damage over time that impairs cellular transcription.
hallmarks_of_aging.disease_reversal_strategy: DNA repair support via sleep, stress reduction, and antioxidant plant compounds.

hallmarks_of_aging.name: Telomere Shortening
hallmarks_of_aging.biological_mechanism: Erosion of protective chromosome ends with successive cell divisions.
hallmarks_of_aging.disease_reversal_strategy: Preserving telomerase activity through stress reduction, restorative sleep, and plant-based nutrition.

hallmarks_of_aging.name: Epigenetic Alterations
hallmarks_of_aging.biological_mechanism: Inappropriate DNA methylation and histone modifications silencing health genes.
hallmarks_of_aging.disease_reversal_strategy: Folate, polyphenols, and lifestyle practices act as biochemical switches turning on longevity genes.

hallmarks_of_aging.name: Loss of Proteostasis
hallmarks_of_aging.biological_mechanism: Failure of protein folding and accumulation of damaged, toxic protein aggregates.
hallmarks_of_aging.disease_reversal_strategy: Exercise and intermittent fasting activate cellular autophagy to recycle damaged proteins.

hallmarks_of_aging.name: Deregulated Nutrient Sensing
hallmarks_of_aging.biological_mechanism: Insulin resistance, mTOR hyperactivation, and blunted AMPK/sirtuin signaling.
hallmarks_of_aging.disease_reversal_strategy: Low-glycemic whole food plant-based nutrition restores metabolic flexibility and insulin sensitivity.

hallmarks_of_aging.name: Mitochondrial Dysfunction
hallmarks_of_aging.biological_mechanism: Decreased ATP output and increased leak of damaging reactive oxygen species (ROS).
hallmarks_of_aging.disease_reversal_strategy: HIIT exercise, fasting, and cofactors (CoQ10, PQQ) trigger mitochondrial biogenesis.

hallmarks_of_aging.name: Cellular Senescence
hallmarks_of_aging.biological_mechanism: Permanently arrested 'zombie' cells secreting pro-inflammatory cytokines (SASP).
hallmarks_of_aging.disease_reversal_strategy: Exercise, polyphenols (quercetin, fisetin), and fasting induce clearance of senescent cells.

hallmarks_of_aging.name: Stem Cell Exhaustion
hallmarks_of_aging.biological_mechanism: Depletion of regenerative stem cell pools in bone marrow, gut, and brain.
hallmarks_of_aging.disease_reversal_strategy: Regular physical activity, restful sleep, and intermittent fasting stimulate stem cell renewal.

hallmarks_of_aging.name: Altered Intercellular Communication
hallmarks_of_aging.biological_mechanism: Systemic chronic 'inflammaging' and neuroendocrine signaling breakdown.
hallmarks_of_aging.disease_reversal_strategy: Anti-inflammatory nutrition, stress regulation, and social connection restore neuro-immune balance.

pillar_hallmark_map.reversal_mechanism: Mediterranean & WFPB diets restore insulin sensitivity and optimal nutrient sensing.
Polyphenols and folate provide methyl donors for favorable epigenetic expression.
Antioxidant-rich nutrition quenches ROS and fuels mitochondrial energy production.
Muscle contraction activates proteasomal degradation and cellular autophagy.
Aerobic and resistance exercise upregulates PGC-1α for mitochondrial regeneration.
Regular exercise clears senescent immune cells and reduces chronic SASP inflammation.
Physical exertion mobilizes endothelial and mesenchymal stem cells for tissue repair.
Deep delta-wave sleep allows enzymatic DNA repair and reduces oxidative double-strand breaks.
Adequate sleep prevents accelerated telomere attrition from chronic fatigue.
Glymphatic brain clearance during slow-wave sleep flushes out amyloid and misfolded proteins.
Cortisol suppression prevents catecholamine-induced oxidative DNA breaks.
Mindfulness and relaxation prevent adverse stress-induced histone modifications.
Vagal nerve stimulation reduces systemic inflammation and normalizes cytokine communication.
Eliminating carcinogens and toxins stops exogenous DNA adduct formation.
Avoiding heavy metals and alcohol prevents mitochondrial membrane permeability transition.
Reducing toxic burden slows the rate at which damaged somatic cells enter senescence.
Social support suppresses pro-inflammatory transcription factors and promotes oxytocin.
Positive relationships buffer social isolation-induced cellular senescence.
Community emotional security supports immune competence and regenerative capacity.

habits_superpowers.tagline: Move your body every day for energy, strong muscles, and mental focus.
habits_superpowers.description: Loves when you move your body daily! Whether walking, dancing, playing sports, or doing yoga, this superhero makes your heart stronger, muscles powerful, and brain sharper.
habits_superpowers.superpower_check_questions: Can you move your body for at least 30 minutes every day? Do you feel strong and energetic?
habits_superpowers.morning_routine: Do 10 jumping jacks or 5 minutes of mobility stretching to activate muscles.
habits_superpowers.meal_guidance: Fuel post-exercise with plant proteins, legumes, and hydration.
habits_superpowers.evening_wind_down: Spend 10 minutes gently moving or walking after dinner to thank your Movement Master.
habits_superpowers.synergistic_helpers: Helps Gut Guardian (improves peristalsis), Energy Maker (creates mitochondria), Sleep Guardian (deepens delta sleep), and Stress Fighter (releases endorphins).

habits_superpowers.tagline: Feed your body vibrant, colorful whole plants to heal inflammation and stabilize blood sugar.
habits_superpowers.description: In charge of all healthy food you eat. Loves colorful fruits, vegetables, healthy plant proteins, and healthy fats that make body and brain work in harmony.
habits_superpowers.superpower_check_questions: Are you eating lots of colorful vegetables and fruits every day? Do you choose foods that make you feel nourished rather than sluggish?
habits_superpowers.morning_routine: Drink a glass of warm lemon water and enjoy berries or oatmeal.
habits_superpowers.meal_guidance: Feed your cells with a colorful rainbow plate: leafy greens, legumes, whole grains, and healthy fats like walnuts/flaxseed.
habits_superpowers.evening_wind_down: Avoid heavy late-night snacking at least 3 hours before sleep.
habits_superpowers.synergistic_helpers: Supports Gut Guardian (provides fiber for microbiome), Energy Maker (clean cellular fuel), Body Protector (detox antioxidants), and Stress Fighter (stable glucose prevents anxiety).

habits_superpowers.tagline: Nurture your microbiome with prebiotics and fermented foods for immunity and mood.
habits_superpowers.description: Protects your tummy and helps you absorb all essential nutrients. Directly connected to the brain via the gut-brain axis; produces over 80% of the body's serotonin for joy and calm.
habits_superpowers.superpower_check_questions: Does your tummy feel comfortable after eating? Do you have regular, smooth bathroom visits? Is your mood calm and stable?
habits_superpowers.morning_routine: Hydrate with clean water before morning meals to awaken digestive enzymes.
habits_superpowers.meal_guidance: Include prebiotic foods (garlic, onion, leeks, asparagus) and fermented foods (kimchi, sauerkraut, kefir).
habits_superpowers.evening_wind_down: Sip soothing chamomile or peppermint tea; allow the gut to rest overnight (12-hour fast).
habits_superpowers.synergistic_helpers: Works with Fuel Captain (processes nutrients), Energy Maker (nutrient absorption), and Stress Fighter (regulates neurotransmitters and gut comfort).

habits_superpowers.tagline: Supercharge your cellular engines to produce clean ATP and all-day vitality.
habits_superpowers.description: Lives inside every single cell turning fuel into ATP energy. When your mitochondria are healthy, you have boundless, steady energy without crashes.
habits_superpowers.superpower_check_questions: Do you have steady energy throughout the day? Do you wake up feeling refreshed and ready to go?
habits_superpowers.morning_routine: Get 5 minutes of morning sunlight in your eyes to sync mitochondrial circadian clocks.
habits_superpowers.meal_guidance: Incorporate antioxidant cofactors: dark berries, green tea, cruciferous greens, and healthy fats.
habits_superpowers.evening_wind_down: Avoid blue light exposure 1 hour before bed to prevent mitochondrial stress.
habits_superpowers.synergistic_helpers: Strengthens Movement Master (fuels muscle output), Sleep Guardian (regulates energy cycles), and Body Protector (resists oxidative damage).

habits_superpowers.tagline: Protect 7–9 hours of deep sleep to repair DNA, balance hormones, and restore mental focus.
habits_superpowers.description: Works tirelessly while you sleep to repair damaged tissues, clean metabolic waste from your brain (glymphatic wash), and reset your neuroendocrine clock.
habits_superpowers.superpower_check_questions: Do you sleep 7–9 hours every night? Do you wake up rested and ready for the day?
habits_superpowers.morning_routine: Wake up at the same consistent time every day; expose eyes to daylight.
habits_superpowers.meal_guidance: Eat lighter evening meals; avoid caffeine after 12 PM and alcohol before bed.
habits_superpowers.evening_wind_down: Wind down 30 minutes before bed: dim lights, read a physical book, practice 4-7-8 breathing.
habits_superpowers.synergistic_helpers: Empowers Energy Maker (recharges cellular engines), Body Protector (boosts natural killer immune cells), and Stress Fighter (keeps amygdala reactive stress low).

habits_superpowers.tagline: Harness breathwork, yoga, and mindfulness to maintain calm and executive control.
habits_superpowers.description: Teaches you to breathe deeply, think positive thoughts, and stay centered during life's pressures. Protects your prefrontal cortex from toxic cortisol spikes.
habits_superpowers.superpower_check_questions: Do you have reliable ways to calm down when stressed? Can you focus clearly and maintain patience?
habits_superpowers.morning_routine: Take 10 deep diaphragmatic breaths upon waking; write down 3 things you are grateful for.
habits_superpowers.meal_guidance: Practice mindful eating without screens or rushing.
habits_superpowers.evening_wind_down: Do 5 minutes of alternate nostril breathing or restorative yoga before bed.
habits_superpowers.synergistic_helpers: Aids Sleep Guardian (calms sympathetic arousal), Gut Guardian (prevents stress-induced leaky gut), and Movement Master (prevents muscle tension).

habits_superpowers.tagline: Cultivate deep friendships, family bonds, and community service to live longer.
habits_superpowers.description: Reminds you that genuine human connection is biological medicine. Loving relationships release oxytocin, lower blood pressure, and build lifelong resilience.
habits_superpowers.superpower_check_questions: Do you have people in your life who care about you? Do you spend meaningful time with friends and family regularly?
habits_superpowers.morning_routine: Send an encouraging message or express gratitude to a friend or loved one.
habits_superpowers.meal_guidance: Share meals with family or colleagues without digital distraction.
habits_superpowers.evening_wind_down: Connect with a partner or friend about your day; practice active empathetic listening.
habits_superpowers.synergistic_helpers: Bolsters Stress Fighter (shared burdens reduce cortisol), Sleep Guardian (emotional peace aids rest), and Body Protector (social support boosts immune antibodies).

habits_superpowers.tagline: Shield your cells from chemicals, pesticides, and pollutants while supporting liver and kidney detox.
habits_superpowers.description: Helps your liver, kidneys, skin, and immune system work together to filter out toxins, fight off infections, and keep your internal biological environment pristine.
habits_superpowers.superpower_check_questions: Is your skin clear and healthy? Do you avoid smoking and excess alcohol? Does your body feel clean and resilient?
habits_superpowers.morning_routine: Drink 16 oz of filtered water immediately upon waking to flush overnight metabolic waste.
habits_superpowers.meal_guidance: Eat cruciferous vegetables (broccoli, cabbage, kale) and drink green tea to stimulate Phase I & II liver detox.
habits_superpowers.evening_wind_down: Take an evening shower or dry brush skin; filter bedroom air.
habits_superpowers.synergistic_helpers: Shields Gut Guardian (protects mucosal barrier), Energy Maker (prevents heavy metal mitochondrial poisoning), and Fuel Captain (absorbs clean nutrition).

ashtanga_limbs.health_impact: Reduces stress, supports social health, lowers chronic systemic inflammation.

ashtanga_limbs.core_focus: Self-discipline, purity/cleanliness (Saucha), gratitude, study, and positive routines.
ashtanga_limbs.health_impact: Builds self-care habits, psychological resilience, and anti-inflammatory lifestyle adherence.

ashtanga_limbs.core_focus: Conscious movement, flexibility, spinal mobility, and strength training.
ashtanga_limbs.health_impact: Improves muscular strength, glucose uptake, mitochondrial biogenesis, and metabolic health.

ashtanga_limbs.core_focus: Rhythmic breath modulation (diaphragmatic, alternate nostril, box breathing).
ashtanga_limbs.health_impact: Lowers sympathetic tone, stimulates vagus nerve, reduces cortisol, and optimizes heart rate variability.

ashtanga_limbs.core_focus: Conscious digital detox, calming sensory overstimulation, mindful hunger awareness.
ashtanga_limbs.health_impact: Reduces reactivity to unhealthy food and stress cues; enhances mindful eating.

ashtanga_limbs.core_focus: Single-pointed focus, eliminating multitasking, cultivating deep mental presence.
ashtanga_limbs.health_impact: Enhances cognitive working memory efficiency, supports sustainable habit building, and relieves anxiety.

ashtanga_limbs.core_focus: Sustained mindful contemplation and awareness without judgment.
ashtanga_limbs.health_impact: Lowers neuro-inflammation, downregulates amygdala hyperactivity, and promotes neuroplastic healing.

ashtanga_limbs.core_focus: Unity of mind, body, and purpose; feeling connected to self and community.
ashtanga_limbs.health_impact: Fosters existential meaning, allostatic peace, emotional resilience, and holistic longevity.

chronic_disease_drivers.microhabit_example: Chew food 20 times before swallowing; practice gentle seated spinal twists after meals.
chronic_disease_drivers.evidence_impact: Improves microbiome diversity, heals mucosal integrity, and reduces systemic endotoxemia.

chronic_disease_drivers.microhabit_example: Log 3 colors of fruits/veggies daily; practice 5 minutes of Nadi Shodhana breathing.

chronic_disease_drivers.microhabit_example: Take a 10-minute brisk walk immediately after dinner; pause before snacking to rate real hunger.
chronic_disease_drivers.evidence_impact: Stimulates GLUT4 glucose transporter translocation independent of insulin, stabilizing glycemia.

chronic_disease_drivers.ashtanga_alignment: Yama: Choose toxin-free products; Asana: Sweating practices
chronic_disease_drivers.microhabit_example: Swap plastic storage containers for glass; take an infrared sauna or brisk sweat-inducing walk.
chronic_disease_drivers.evidence_impact: Enhances Phase I/II liver biotransformation and reduces environmental xenobiotic burden.

chronic_disease_drivers.ashtanga_alignment: Pranayama: Evening breathwork; Asana: Endocrine-supportive poses
chronic_disease_drivers.microhabit_example: Practice 4-7-8 breathing before bed; do legs-up-the-wall (Viparita Karani) to calm adrenals.
chronic_disease_drivers.evidence_impact: Normalizes circadian cortisol rhythm, balances thyroid hormones, and supports reproductive vitality.

chronic_disease_drivers.ashtanga_alignment: Niyama: Gratitude practice; Dhyana: Meditation on healing
chronic_disease_drivers.microhabit_example: Write down 3 specific things you are grateful for each morning; meditate for 10 minutes.
chronic_disease_drivers.evidence_impact: Provides favorable biochemical signals that upregulate longevity genes and downregulate oncogenes.

chronic_disease_drivers.ashtanga_alignment: Asana: HIIT / dynamic yoga; Niyama: Antioxidant-rich foods
chronic_disease_drivers.microhabit_example: Incorporate short bursts of bodyweight squats/HIIT 3x weekly; eat blueberries and green tea.
chronic_disease_drivers.evidence_impact: Stimulates endogenous circulating stem cell mobilization and cellular tissue regeneration.

chronic_disease_drivers.ashtanga_alignment: Asana: Brisk walking / HIIT; Pranayama: Breathwork for oxygenation
chronic_disease_drivers.microhabit_example: Walk briskly outdoors for 20 minutes; practice deep diaphragmatic breath cycles.
chronic_disease_drivers.evidence_impact: Stimulates PGC-1α-driven mitochondrial biogenesis and enhances cellular ATP generation.

my_goal_do_it_steps.description: Set a clear, heartfelt daily intention that connects your habit to your life purpose.
my_goal_do_it_steps.behavioral_science_principle: Autonomous motivation theory (Ryan & Deci) — habits linked to identity endure.

my_goal_do_it_steps.description: Pick a microhabit tailored specifically to your preferences and daily rhythm.
my_goal_do_it_steps.behavioral_science_principle: Self-determination theory — personal autonomy maximizes behavioral adherence.

my_goal_do_it_steps.description: Define the exact, measurable, bite-sized action (e.g., 'walk 10 minutes after lunch').
my_goal_do_it_steps.behavioral_science_principle: Implementation intentions (Gollwitzer) — clear 'if-then' plans double success rate.

my_goal_do_it_steps.description: Focus on mastering one tiny microhabit before adding another.
my_goal_do_it_steps.behavioral_science_principle: Cognitive load reduction — avoids willpower exhaustion and decision fatigue.

my_goal_do_it_steps.description: Attach the new microhabit to an established daily anchor (e.g., 'after brushing teeth, do 10 squats').
my_goal_do_it_steps.behavioral_science_principle: Habit stacking (BJ Fogg Tiny Habits) — piggybacks on existing neural pathways.

my_goal_do_it_steps.description: Design your physical and social environment so healthy choices are frictionless.
my_goal_do_it_steps.behavioral_science_principle: Choice architecture (Thaler & Sunstein) — environment is the invisible hand shaping behavior.

my_goal_do_it_steps.description: Practice the microhabit every day without exception, keeping the barrier to entry minimal.
my_goal_do_it_steps.behavioral_science_principle: Neuroplasticity — daily repetition builds automatic basal ganglia habit loops.

my_goal_do_it_steps.description: When friction arises, pause, breathe deeply, and adjust rather than quit.
my_goal_do_it_steps.behavioral_science_principle: Emotional regulation & resilience — prevents the 'what-the-hell' relapse effect.

my_goal_do_it_steps.description: Celebrate every win and identify as a healthy, vibrant individual.
my_goal_do_it_steps.behavioral_science_principle: Identity-based habits (James Clear) — 'I am someone who nourishes my cells daily'.

my_goal_do_it_steps.description: Log your progress in a journal and teach someone else the principle.
my_goal_do_it_steps.behavioral_science_principle: Social accountability & Feynman learning technique — teaching solidifies mastery.

quiz_questions.question_text: Do your parents, brothers, or sisters have type 2 diabetes?
Is your waist circumference greater than 40 inches (men) or 35 inches (women)?
Do you frequently feel tired, drowsy, or sleepy 30–60 minutes after eating meals?
Do you frequently crave refined carbohydrates, bread, chips, or sugary sweets?
Do you notice dark velvety skin patches on your neck/armpits (acanthosis nigricans) or skin tags?
Has a physician told you that your blood pressure is high (≥ 130/85 mmHg)?
Do blood tests show elevated triglycerides (≥ 150 mg/dL) or low HDL cholesterol (< 40 men, < 50 women)?
Is it difficult to lose weight, particularly stubborn fat accumulating around your belly?
Have you ever been diagnosed with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) or PCOS?
Do you experience frequent urination, excessive thirst, or episodes of blurry vision?
Have you experienced changes in your menstrual cycle (women) or diminished libido/drive (men/women)?
Do you struggle with frequent unexplained mood swings, anxiety, or irritability?
Do you have a personal or family history of thyroid dysfunction (hypo/hyperthyroidism)?
Do you frequently feel cold when others are comfortable, or have chronically cold hands/feet?
Have you noticed unexplained weight gain or an inability to lose weight despite dieting?
Do you have difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or wake up unrefreshed?
Are you experiencing diffuse hair thinning, loss, or unexpected facial/body hair growth?
Do you suffer from frequent hot flashes, night sweats, or temperature dysregulation?
Have you developed sudden changes in skin texture, adult acne, or excessive dryness?
Are you currently taking any prescription hormone therapies, birth control, or hormone supplements?
Do you regularly consume ultra-processed foods, fast food, or food packaged in plastics?
Do you routinely use conventional aerosol sprays, synthetic perfumes, or scented lotions?
Are you frequently exposed to air pollution, agricultural pesticides, mold, or older paint?
Do you smoke, vape, or regularly breathe second-hand tobacco or cannabis smoke?
Do you consume alcoholic drinks more than 1–2 times per week?
Do you use recreational drugs or take frequent over-the-counter NSAIDs/pain medications?
Do you drink unfiltered municipal tap water or water from thin plastic bottles?
Are you taking multiple daily pharmaceutical drugs that stress liver or renal pathways?
Have you experienced chronic fatigue, skin rashes, or brain fog that doesn't resolve?
Does your family have a significant history of early cancer, neurodegenerative, or autoimmune disease?
How often do you experience bloating, abdominal distension, or gas after meals?

quiz_questions.question_text: Does anyone in your family (parents/siblings) have early type 2 diabetes, heart disease, or cancer?
Are you frequently around environmental pollution, cigarette smoke, or chemical fumes?
Do you feel emotionally stressed, anxious, or pressured on most days of the week?
Do you consume fewer than 2 full servings of vegetables and fruits on most days?
Do you routinely sleep less than 7 hours per night or have fragmented sleep?
Do you get less than 30 minutes of physical activity or walking on most days?
Did you experience significant adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) or severe early life trauma?
Do you drink sugar-sweetened beverages, sports drinks, or alcohol more than twice a week?
Do you frequently drink from soft plastic bottles or handle thermal paper receipts?
Is it challenging to maintain a healthy body composition or stable weight?
Low Energy: Do you often feel drained or lack sustained stamina throughout the day?
Brain Fog: Is it hard to concentrate, think quickly, or maintain sharp mental clarity?
Muscle Performance: Do you experience muscle weakness, exercise intolerance, or slow recovery?
Metabolic Concerns: Have you been diagnosed with insulin resistance, obesity, or fatty liver?
Toxin Exposure: Have you had known exposure to heavy metals, mold, or organic pollutants?
Diet Quality: Is your diet low in colorful berries, polyphenols, and antioxidant-rich vegetables?
Headaches: Do you suffer from frequent unexplained headaches or migraines?
Sensory Changes: Have you noticed accelerated changes in visual acuity or hearing?
Temperature Regulation: Do you struggle to maintain a comfortable body temperature?
Medication Effects: Are you on medications known to stress mitochondria (statins, certain antibiotics)?
Do you take an unusually long time to bounce back or recover after strenuous physical exertion?
Are small skin cuts, bruises, or surgical wounds noticeably slow to heal?
Is your hair thinning rapidly or greying significantly earlier than expected?
Do you catch frequent seasonal colds, infections, or take weeks to clear common bugs?
Do you experience persistent brain fog or notice your memory is not as sharp as it was?
Are you losing muscle tone or strength despite doing normal daily activities?
Have you been diagnosed with chronic autoimmune conditions or persistent joint inflammation?
Do you have chronic tummy trouble, irregular bowel habits, or food intolerances?
Has your weight fluctuated dramatically up or down without intentional dieting?
Do you spend more than 8 hours of your waking day sitting and physically inactive?
Are you subjected to chronic unmanaged stress, ultra-processed diet, or poor sleep?

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Low Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Optimal insulin sensitivity. Minimal evidence of metabolic resistance.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Maintain colorful plant-forward diet, 150 min/wk physical activity, and routine annual metabolic lab screening.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Moderate Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Early metabolic strain. Elevated risk of progressing to pre-diabetes and metabolic syndrome.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Implement 10-minute post-meal walks, prioritize fiber-first meals, eliminate liquid sugars, and request fasting insulin + lipid panel.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: High Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Significant insulin resistance. High probability of pre-diabetes, visceral adiposity, and metabolic inflammation.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Consult physician for complete metabolic workup (HbA1c, fasting insulin, HOMA-IR, lipid profile, liver panel). Adopt strict whole-food plant-based diet and supervised lifestyle protocol.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Minimal Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Healthy neuroendocrine balance. Endocrine feedback loops operating well.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Protect consistent sleep schedules (bed by 10 PM), manage daily stress with breathwork, and maintain micronutrient-dense diet.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Medium Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Mild to moderate neuroendocrine imbalance affecting thyroid, adrenal cortisol, or sex hormone balance.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Adopt evening wind-down routine to lower cortisol, reduce caffeine and alcohol, increase cruciferous vegetables for estrogen metabolism, and discuss hormone labs with doctor.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: High Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Pronounced hormone disruption significantly impairing sleep, metabolism, and mood.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Comprehensive laboratory evaluation (TSH, Free T3/T4, Cortisol, DHEA-S, sex hormones). Work with an integrative/functional medicine doctor on targeted nutrition and adaptogens.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Mild Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Low environmental xenobiotic exposure and adequate biological detoxification reserve.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Continue filtered drinking water, eat organic produce where possible, and use clean household personal care products.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Moderate Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Substantial ongoing exposure to environmental chemicals, processed packaging, or lifestyle toxins.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Transition food storage from plastic to glass, drink filtered water, add cruciferous vegetables (sulforaphane) to support Phase II liver detox, and sweat weekly.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Severe Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Heavy toxic burden overwhelming hepatic and renal detoxification pathways.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Work with clinical team to perform detox lab testing (heavy metals, environmental toxins, liver enzymes). Eliminate smoking/alcohol and implement structured lifestyle detox protocol.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Awesome Gut Health
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Robust microbiome diversity, healthy mucosal barrier, and optimal digestion.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Keep enjoying at least 30 diverse plant foods weekly, fermented foods, and staying well hydrated.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Gut Needs TLC
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Early microbial dysbiosis, mild permeability, or dietary fiber deficiency.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Chew thoroughly (20x/bite), increase prebiotic foods (garlic, onions, asparagus), include daily probiotic foods, and avoid eating under stress.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Moderate Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Significant gut dysbiosis causing chronic digestive complaints, fatigue, and systemic inflammation.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Eliminate the 'six poisons' (refined sugar, processed food, dairy, gluten, trans fats). Consider gentle herbal support (ginger, peppermint, licorice) and consult gut specialist.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: High Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Severe gastrointestinal impairment, marked dysbiosis, and compromised gut-brain communication.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Consult healthcare provider for comprehensive stool testing (GI-MAP/microbiome), food sensitivity testing, and clinical gut restoration protocol (Remove, Replace, Reinoculate, Repair).

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Mild Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Favorable epigenetic signaling. Daily lifestyle choices support longevity gene expression.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Continue daily movement, restorative sleep, colorful nutrition, and positive stress-reduction routines.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Moderate Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Sub-optimal lifestyle habits are triggering pro-inflammatory epigenetic pathways.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Incorporate folate-rich foods (spinach, lentils, asparagus) to support DNA methylation, reduce chemical exposures, and commit to daily mindfulness.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Severe Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: High allostatic burden driving accelerated biological aging and adverse gene transcription.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Structured lifestyle intervention across all 6 lifestyle medicine pillars. Consider biological age testing (epigenetic DNA methylation clock) and personalized physician coaching.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Low Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Mitochondrial density and ATP generation are robust and well-maintained.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Maintain regular aerobic activity, antioxidant-rich whole foods, and consistent circadian rhythms.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Moderate Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Mitochondrial efficiency is lagging, leading to brain fog, fatigue, and slow recovery.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Add high-intensity interval training (HIIT) to stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis (PGC-1α), get morning sunlight, and consider cofactors (CoQ10, alpha-lipoic acid, magnesium).

quiz_scoring_rules.label: High Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Substantial mitochondrial dysfunction with elevated oxidative stress and cellular bioenergetic deficit.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Medical evaluation including metabolic labs (lactate, pyruvate, CK, CMP, lipid profile). Implement targeted mitochondrial therapy and clinical antioxidant support.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Low Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Regenerative stem cell pools and tissue repair mechanisms are thriving.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Keep up healthy plant nutrition, regular exercise, deep sleep, and active stress management.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: Moderate Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Accelerated cellular wear and tear depleting endogenous stem cell renewal.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Incorporate safe intermittent fasting or time-restricted eating, eat polyphenol-rich foods (berries, green tea), and commit to 7-9 hours of nightly restorative sleep.

quiz_scoring_rules.label: High Risk
quiz_scoring_rules.clinical_interpretation: Severe stem cell exhaustion and compromised regenerative resilience.
quiz_scoring_rules.recommended_actions: Work with a longevity medicine physician. Conduct comprehensive biomarker panel (telomere length, inflammatory cytokines, cellular health panels) and aggressive lifestyle rejuvenation.

therapeutic_supplements.name: Curcumin (Turmeric)
therapeutic_supplements.mechanism_and_evidence: Potent inhibitor of NF-κB, COX-2, and inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-6). Reduces joint pain and cartilage breakdown.
therapeutic_supplements.typical_dosage_and_notes: 500–2,000 mg/day (standardized to 95% curcuminoids, enhanced with piperine/black pepper extract for 2000% bioavailability).
therapeutic_supplements.primary_indications: Chronic inflammation, osteoarthritis, metabolic syndrome, gut permeability.

therapeutic_supplements.name: Omega-3 Fatty Acids (EPA/DHA)
therapeutic_supplements.mechanism_and_evidence: Precursor to specialized pro-resolving mediators (resolvins, protectins). Lowers triglycerides, CRP, and cardiovascular risk.
therapeutic_supplements.typical_dosage_and_notes: 1,000–4,000 mg/day of combined EPA/DHA from molecularly distilled fish oil or algae oil.
therapeutic_supplements.primary_indications: Cardiovascular risk, elevated triglycerides, brain health, arthritis, neuro-inflammation.

therapeutic_supplements.name: Ginger (Zingiber officinale)
therapeutic_supplements.mechanism_and_evidence: Inhibits cyclooxygenase and lipoxygenase pathways, reducing leukotrienes and prostaglandins.
therapeutic_supplements.primary_indications: Digestive discomfort, nausea, joint stiffness, exercise-induced muscle soreness.

therapeutic_supplements.name: Boswellia serrata (Frankincense)
therapeutic_supplements.mechanism_and_evidence: Blocks 5-lipoxygenase (5-LOX) pro-inflammatory enzyme; preserves connective tissue glycosaminoglycans.
therapeutic_supplements.primary_indications: Osteoarthritis, back pain, inflammatory bowel complaints, asthma.

therapeutic_supplements.name: Quercetin
therapeutic_supplements.mechanism_and_evidence: Flavonoid antioxidant with senolytic properties; stabilizes mast cells, inhibits histamine release, and supports zinc ionophore uptake.
therapeutic_supplements.typical_dosage_and_notes: 200–500 mg/day (often paired with bromelain or vitamin C).
therapeutic_supplements.primary_indications: Cellular senescence, seasonal allergies, vascular endothelitis, longevity.

therapeutic_supplements.name: Coenzyme Q10 (Ubiquinol)
therapeutic_supplements.mechanism_and_evidence: Essential electron carrier in mitochondrial respiratory chain (Complexes I, II, III). Potent lipophilic antioxidant.
therapeutic_supplements.primary_indications: Mitochondrial dysfunction, statin-induced myopathy, heart failure, cognitive fatigue.

therapeutic_supplements.name: Magnesium (Glycinate / Malate / Threonate)
therapeutic_supplements.mechanism_and_evidence: Cofactor in > 300 enzymatic reactions including ATP synthesis, DNA repair, and muscle relaxation.
therapeutic_supplements.primary_indications: Insomnia, muscle cramps, anxiety, hypertension, insulin resistance.

therapeutic_supplements.name: Berberine
therapeutic_supplements.mechanism_and_evidence: Activates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), mimics caloric restriction, lowers glucose and LDL cholesterol.
therapeutic_supplements.primary_indications: Insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, gut dysbiosis.

therapeutic_supplements.name: Alpha-Lipoic Acid (ALA)
therapeutic_supplements.mechanism_and_evidence: Universal water- and fat-soluble antioxidant; regenerates glutathione, vitamin C, and coenzyme Q10.
therapeutic_supplements.primary_indications: Diabetic neuropathy, insulin sensitivity, mitochondrial protection.

therapeutic_supplements.name: PQQ (Pyrroloquinoline Quinone)
therapeutic_supplements.mechanism_and_evidence: Stimulates mitochondrial biogenesis via CREB phosphorylation and PGC-1α activation.
therapeutic_supplements.primary_indications: Cellular aging, cognitive decline, mitochondrial renewal.

lab_biomarkers.clinical_significance: Evaluates baseline hepatic enzymes (AST/ALT), kidney filtration (BUN/Creatinine), fasting blood glucose, and electrolyte balance.
Assesses red blood cells, hemoglobin, white blood cell sub-types, and platelet count to screen for anemia and infection.
Measures Total Cholesterol, Triglycerides, HDL, LDL, and Non-HDL cholesterol to evaluate atherogenic risk.
Measures percentage of glycated hemoglobin; standard clinical diagnostic marker for pre-diabetes (5.7–6.4%) and diabetes (≥ 6.5%).
Acute phase reactant synthesized by liver in response to IL-6. Scores < 1.0 mg/L represent low systemic vascular inflammation.
Non-specific rate of red blood cell settling; elevated in autoimmune conditions, infection, and chronic inflammation.
Detects compensatory hyperinsulinemia years before fasting blood glucose rises; used to compute HOMA-IR index.
Elevated lactate/pyruvate ratio indicates impaired mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation and shift to anaerobic glycolysis.
Screens for myopathy, muscle damage from statins, or metabolic muscle disease.
Hormone precursor regulating thousands of genes. Optimal longevity target is 50–80 ng/mL.

lab_biomarkers.test_name: Epigenetic DNA Methylation Age Clock (GrimAge / Horvath)
lab_biomarkers.clinical_significance: Analyzes CpG island methylation patterns across the genome to measure biological pace of aging and mortality risk.
Quantifies mean terminal restriction fragment length of telomeres to benchmark cellular age against age-matched controls.
Quantifies abundance of keystone bacteria (Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Akkermansia muciniphila) and detects dysbiosis or zonulin leaks.
Measures urinary organic acid metabolites reflecting Krebs cycle efficiency, neurotransmitter turnover, and yeast/bacterial overgrowth.
Urinary or blood analysis of phthalates, parabens, organophosphates, lead, mercury, arsenic, and cadmium.
